subject: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding
messages:
From: Michael Rowe <michael.rowe@aegisbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aegis Bank Procurement <procure@aegisbank.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Hi Vivek / Karthik,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Procurement asked me to consolidate the onboarding steps for the RFI we shared — they want a single point of contact and a clear artifact intake plan. Specifically: a control-to-evidence crosswalk for SIG + SOC 2, an expected delivery cadence, and any pre-approved redaction guidance for sensitive attachments.

Can you confirm who will be our intake lead, what artifacts you can provide within 5 business days, and whether you have a secure upload method (SFTP/portal) we should use?

Appreciate a short plan so we can present it to legal and our compliance team on Wednesday.

Best,
Michael
Michael Rowe
Procurement Manager, Aegis Bank
procure@aegisbank.com

---
Attachment: RFI_Aegis_Initial.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Michael Rowe <michael.rowe@aegisbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Michael — thanks for outlining. Short answers below and a proposed intake plan attached.

Intake lead: Karthik Iyer (Security & Assurance) — he will own the crosswalk and artifact collection.
Secure upload: We can provision a time-limited transfer link to our secure portal (SAML + client cert) or accept uploads via encrypted SFTP. We will send a portal invite and temporary bucket credentials by EOD.
What we can deliver in 5 business days: a preliminary control map (SIG v3.1 -> SOC 2 CC -> ISO 27001 clause) and a list of required artifacts from our side with tentative delivery dates. Evidence delivery (actual artifacts) depends on custodian approvals.

Attached: evidence_mapping_v1.xlsx (control map + proposed artifact owners). I also included a recommended redaction checklist for customer-facing artifacts.

Next steps: Karthik will follow up with a detailed owner schedule and a link to the secure upload. If procurement requires DocuSign or an NDA amendment, loop Marissa.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

---
Attachment: evidence_mapping_v1.xlsx (worksheet stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Rowe <michael.rowe@aegisbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Michael — assigning details below and a proposed 3-phase intake cadence so compliance has clarity.

Phase 0 (same day): Portal invite + temporary upload credentials (expires in 7 days). We will provide an SSO link and upload instructions.

Phase 1 (3 business days): Control crosswalk deliverable (spreadsheet) mapping each SIG control to our SOC 2 CC implementation description and ISO 27001 clause references. This will also include a curated list of artifacts we expect to provide (logs, policies, architecture diagrams, key rotation records).

Phase 2 (7–14 business days): Artifact packet delivery window — we will provide copies of artifacts where permissible (redacted as needed), and for items that are operationally restricted we will provide signed attestations and audit extracts.

Owner matrix (high level):
- Karthik Iyer — control mapping, evidence collation, and security attestations
- Jasmine Liu — compliance packaging, SOC 2-specific artifacts, and evidence redaction guidance
- Marissa Cole — legal/procurement coordination and contract amendments (if necessary)

We recommend starting with a scoped SIG subset (e.g., Access, Encryption, Change Management) so the initial packet is small and actionable. Once Aegis confirms priority areas, we will prioritize artifact pulls.

I will send the portal link and a short how-to by EOD.

Regards,
Karthik
Senior Manager, Security & Assurance
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
Attachment: (none)

From: Michael Rowe <michael.rowe@aegisbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Aegis Bank Procurement <procure@aegisbank.com>
Date: 2028-09-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Thanks Karthik — that cadence looks sensible. A couple of quick clarifications from our compliance team:
1) Can you confirm whether your SOC 2 report (Type II) covers the period Jan–Dec 2027 and whether the report contains a KMS key rotation control description?
2) For any aggregated logs you provide, we will need a statement of retention policy and a sample log export (time-limited).
3) Procurement asked whether your team can provide an initial subset of artifacts for Access Controls and Encryption within the first 5 business days; if so, we can lock those as priority.

If you can confirm 1–3, we will schedule a short bridge call on Friday to align on owners and the upload method.

-Michael

Date: 2028-09-04T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Michael — quick answers inline below and a couple of artifacts attached.

1) SOC 2 Type II coverage: Yes — coverage period Jan 1, 2027 – Dec 31, 2027. We will provide the auditor's cover letter and the control matrix page for the period.

2) Log retention statement: We retain operational request logs for 90 days and anonymized telemetry aggregates for 2 years. I attached a sample log export (sanitized) and a short retention policy excerpt.

3) Access & Encryption subset: We can push a prioritized packet for Access Controls and Encryption within 5 business days. That packet will include: user access reviews, MFA configuration screenshots, KMS key rotation SOP excerpt, and network topology diagram. For KMS key rotation proof, we will provide rotation timestamps and a signed attestation if the raw key material cannot be shared.

Attached: network_flow_v2.png, sop_kms_rotation.pdf (redacted SOP snippet), sample_log_export_sanitized.csv (sanitized log stub).

Let me know if Aegis prefers the artifacts zipped or uploaded individually.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

---
Attachments: network_flow_v2.png (image stub), sop_kms_rotation.pdf (pdf stub)

Subject: Re: AegisBank RFI: SIG/ISO/SOC2 artifact intake and onboarding

Jasmine — this is excellent and exactly what we need to get the compliance review started. A few follow-ups from legal: please include a brief note in the delivery packet that highlights any third-party subprocessors handling customer data (names + regions). Also, procurement prefers the initial Access & Encryption packet as a single zip with the control crosswalk included as the top-level file.

We will accept the Redwood secure portal link (please invite 'security-portal@aegisbank.com' and 'procure@aegisbank.com' as read-only users). Once we see the packet, compliance will triage and flag any evidence gaps within 3 business days.

If you can confirm the portal invite and that the zip will be ready by EOD Monday (2028-09-10), we'll lock the Friday bridge call off our calendar.

Thanks again — looking forward to the packet.

Best,
Michael Rowe
Procurement Manager, Aegis Bank
procure@aegisbank.com
